paragraphs.text: “Most distant part.” Or, “extremity.” Gr., e·skhaʹtou; J17,18,22(Heb.), qetsehʹ. See Jer 25:31, 33 ftns. Compare Mt 12:42 ftn.
Lit., “heaven.” Gr., ou·ra·nonʹ; Lat., caeʹlum; J17(Heb.), hash·sha·ma·yemahʹ, “toward the heaven.”
According to rabbinical sources based on Jos 3:4, this was about 2,000 cubits (890 m; 2,920 ft).
“Office of oversight.” Gr., e·pi·sko·penʹ; J17,18(Heb.), u·phequd·da·thohʹ (from pa·qadhʹ). See 2Ki 11:18 ftn.
That is, about 9 a.m., counting from sunrise.
Or, “active force.” Gr., pneuʹma·tos; Lat., Spiʹri·tu; J17,18,22(Heb.), ru·chiʹ, “my spirit.” See Ge 1:2 ftn, “Force.”
Or, “upon all flesh.” Gr., e·piʹ paʹsan sarʹka; Lat., carʹnem; J17,18,22(Heb.), ba·sarʹ.
Or, “fastened on a stake (pole).” See App 5C.
Lit., “to the breaking of the bread.”
Or, “from house to house.” Gr., katʼ oiʹkon. See 5:42 ftn, “House.”
That is, about 3 p.m., counting from sunrise.
“Jehovah,” J7,8,10-18,20,22-24 and LXXP. Fouad Inv. 266 in De 18:15; Gr., Kyʹri·os. See App 1D.
Or, “fastened on a stake (pole).” See App 5C.
“Sovereign Lord.” Gr., Deʹspo·ta; Lat., Doʹmi·ne; J17,18(Heb.), ʼAdho·naiʹ. See App 1E.
Lit., “filled your heart.” See Es 7:5; Ec 8:11.
Lit., “ecclesia.” Gr., ek·kle·siʹan; Lat., ec·cleʹsi·a; J17,18(Heb.), haq·qa·halʹ, “the congregation.”
Or, “tree.” Gr., xyʹlou; J22(Heb.), ʽets. See 2:36 ftn.

Lit., “according to house.” Gr., katʼ oiʹkon. Here ka·taʹ is used with the accusative sing. in the distributive sense. R. C. H. Lenski, in his work The Interpretation of The Acts of the Apostles, Minneapolis (1961), made the following comment on Ac 5:42: “Never for a moment did the apostles cease their blessed work. ‘Every day’ they continued, and this openly ‘in the Temple’ where the Sanhedrin and the Temple police could see and hear them, and, of course, also κατ’ οἴκον, which is distributive, ‘from house to house,’ and not merely adverbial, ‘at home.’ ”
Or, “declaring the evangel (gospel).” Gr., eu·ag·ge·li·zoʹme·noi; Lat., e·van·ge·li·zanʹtes, “evangelizing.”
Lit., “of the Hellenists.” Gr., ton Hel·le·ni·stonʹ; Lat., Grae·coʹrum.
Lit., “the Hebrews.” Gr., tous E·braiʹous; Lat., He·braeʹos.
Or, “in the . . . ministration.” Gr., en tei di·a·ko·niʹai; Lat., in mi·ni·steʹri·o.
Or, “to be ministering.” Gr., di·a·ko·neinʹ; Lat., mi·ni·straʹre.
Lit., “He,” referring to the “God of glory” in vs 2.
“Will render sacred service.” Gr., la·treuʹsou·sinʹ; J17,18,22(Heb.), weya·ʽav·dhuʹni, “and they will serve (worship) me.” See Ex 3:12 ftn.
“Race.” Gr., geʹnos; different from ge·ne·aʹ, “generation,” as in Mt 24:34.
Or, “extremely beautiful.” Lit., “beautiful to the God.” Gr., a·steiʹos toi The·oiʹ. Compare Jon 3:3 ftn, “God.”
“An angel,” P74אABCVg; DSyp, “an angel of [the] Lord”; J7,8,10-17, “Jehovah’s angel.”
Or, “and redeemer.” Gr., kai ly·tro·tenʹ; Lat., et re·dem·ptoʹrem; J17(Heb.), wegho·ʼelʹ.
“God,” אABVg; CSyp, “The Lord God”; J7,8,10-17, “Jehovah your God.”

Lit., “the Law as transmissions of angels.” J17, “the Law at the hands of messenger angels”; Lat., leʹgem in dis·po·si·ti·oʹnem an·ge·loʹrum, “the Law by the disposition of angels.” In 2Ch 23:18 Vg uses dis·po·si·ti·oʹnem in the translation “by the hands of.”
“Jehovah,” J18,22,23; Gr., tou Ky·riʹou; VgSyp, “God.” See App 1D.
“Jehovah,” J7,8,10,13,15-18,22,23; אAB(Gr.), ton Kyʹri·on; DVgmssSyh,p, “God.” See App 1D.
“Of Jehovah,” J7,8,10,17,18; אBCD(Gr.), tou Ky·riʹou; P74ASyp, “of God.” See App 1D.
P45,74אABCVgSyp omit vs 37; ItVgcArm, “Philip said to him: ‘If you believe with all your heart, it is permissible.’ In reply he said: ‘I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.’ ”
Or, “a centurion,” in command of 100 soldiers.
That is, about 3 p.m., counting from sunrise.
That is, about 12 noon, counting from sunrise.
“Was given divine instructions,” אAB; J18, “was given a command of Jehovah.”
“Jehovah,” J17,18,23; P45אABC(Gr.), tou Ky·riʹou; P74DSyp, “God.” See App 1D.
“Christians.” Gr., Khri·sti·a·nousʹ; Lat., Chri·sti·aʹni; J17,18,22(Heb.), Meshi·chi·yimʹ, “Messianists.”
Or, “they began presenting themselves.” Lit., “they were alongside.”
“Of Jehovah,” J7,8,10,23; B(Gr.), tou Ky·riʹou; P74אADSyp, “of God.” See App 1D.
Lit., “the tetrarch,” a territorial prince for the emperor.
A provincial governor for the Roman Senate.
“During about four hundred and fifty years. And after these things,” P74אABCVg.
Or, “What you suppose I am I am not.”
“Who worshiped (feared) God,” Syp; J18, “who feared Jehovah.”
“Of Jehovah,” J17,22; P74אABc(Gr.), tou Ky·riʹou; B*CSyh,p, “of God.” See App 1D.
“Extremity.” Or, “most distant part.” Gr., e·skhaʹtou. See 1:8 ftn, “Part.”
“Of Jehovah,” J7,8,10,13,15-17,22,23; P45,74אAC(Gr.), tou Ky·riʹou; BD, “of God.” See App 1D.
“Who worshiped (feared) God,” Syp; J7,8,10,18, “who feared Jehovah.”
“Word,” BD; אACVgSyp, “word of the Lord”; P74, “word of God”; J17, “word of Jehovah.”
Or, “elders.” Gr., pre·sby·teʹrous; J17,18,22(Heb.), wehaz·zeqe·nimʹ, “and the older men.” See Nu 11:25 ftn, “Men.”
Lit., “turning upon.” Gr., e·pi·stro·phenʹ; Lat., con·ver·si·oʹnem.
A Heb. form of the name Simon (Peter). See Mt 10:2 ftn.
Or, “upon whom my name has been called.”
Or, “who has been making these things (18) known from of old.”
Lit., “to be abstaining.” Gr., a·peʹkhe·sthai; Lat., ab·stiʹne·ant.
“Fornication.” Gr., por·neiʹas; Lat., for·ni·ca·ti·oʹne. See App 5A.
Or, “from what is killed without draining its blood.”
“Blood.” Gr., haiʹma·tos; Lat., sanʹgui·ne; J17,18,22(Heb.), u·min-had·damʹ, “and from the blood.”
Lit., “like-mindedly.” Gr., ho·mo·thy·ma·donʹ; Lat., in uʹnum, “in unity.”
Or, “lives.” Gr., psy·khasʹ; Lat., aʹni·mas; J17,18,22(Heb.), naph·shamʹ, “their souls.”
Or, “Farewell!” J22(Heb.), sha·lohmʹ la·khemʹ, “May you have peace!”
P74אAB omit vs 34; CDVgc add, with variations, “But it seemed good to Silas to remain there further; however Judas alone departed for Jerusalem.”
“Of Jehovah,” J17,18,22,23; Gr., tou Ky·riʹou; Syp, “of God.” See App 1D.
“Of Jehovah,” J7,8,10,17,18,22,23; Gr., tou Ky·riʹou; Syp, “of God.” See App 1D.
“Of Jehovah,” J17,18,22; Gr., tou Ky·riʹou; Vgc,sSyp, “of God.” See App 1D.
“Declare the good news.” Gr., eu·ag·ge·liʹsa·sthai; Lat., e·van·ge·li·zaʹre.
“To Jehovah,” J7,8,10; אAB(Gr.), toi Ky·riʹoi; D, “to God.” See App 1D.
Lit., “with a spirit of python.” Gr., eʹkhou·san pneuʹma pyʹtho·na.
Or, “forum.” Gr., a·go·ranʹ; Lat., foʹrum. A place of public gatherings.
“Of Jehovah,” J7,8,10,17,18,22,23; P45,74אcAC(Gr.), tou Ky·riʹou; א*B, “of God.” See App 1D.
Lit., “politarchs.” Gr., po·li·tarʹkhas, governors of the citizens.
Or, “Hill of Ares; Mars’ Hill.” Gr., Aʹrei·on Paʹgon; Lat., A·ri·oʹpa·gum.

“More given to the fear of the deities.” Lit., “more demon-dreading.” Gr., dei·si·dai·mo·ne·steʹrous; Lat., su·per·sti·ti·o·si·oʹres. Demons were thought by the Greeks to be deities, good or evil. Compare 25:19 ftn.
Or, “divine habitations (dwellings).” Gr., na·oisʹ; J17,22(Heb.), beheh·kha·lohthʹ, “in palaces (temples).”
“Certain ones,” namely, Aratus and Cleanthes. Paul’s quotation is from Phænomena, by Aratus, and from Hymn to Zeus, by Cleanthes.
“Divine Being.” Gr., Theiʹon, related to The·osʹ, “God”; Lat., Di·viʹnum.
“Inhabited earth.” Lit., “inhabited.” Gr., oi·kou·meʹnen, fem. sing., referring to the earth; Lat., orʹbem, “circle,” that is, of the earth. See Isa 13:11 ftn, “Land.”
A provincial governor for the Roman Senate.
The Roman province of southern Greece with its capital at Corinth.
DItmss add: “from the fifth hour to the tenth,” that is, from about 11 a.m. to about 4 p.m.
“Of Jehovah,” J7,8,10,13,15-18,23; Gr., tou Ky·riʹou; VgSyp, “of God.” See App 1D.
“The Way,” אAB; Vgc, “the way of the Lord”; Syp, “the way of God”; J17,18, “Jehovah’s way.”
Or, “divine habitations (dwellings).” Gr., na·ousʹ; J17(Heb.), heh·khelohthʹ, “palaces; temples.”
“That fell from heaven.” Lit., “fallen from Zeus (Jupiter).”
Or, “and in private houses.” Lit., “and according to houses.” Gr., kai katʼ oiʹkous. Here ka·taʹ is used with the accusative pl. in the distributive sense. Compare 5:42 ftn, “House.”
Or, “heralding.” Gr., ke·rysʹson; Lat., praeʹdi·cans. Compare Da 5:29 ftn, “Heralded.”
“Kingdom,” אAB; VgSyp, “kingdom of God”; J17, “kingdom of Jehovah.”
“Overseers.” Gr., e·pi·skoʹpous; J17(Heb.), liph·qi·dhimʹ, “as overseers.” See Ne 11:9 ftn.
For a discussion of “the blood of his own [Son]” see App 6C.
“An apostasy.” Gr., a·po·sta·siʹan (from the verb a·phiʹste·mi, “stand away from”). The noun has the sense of desertion, abandonment or rebellion. See Jos 22:22; 2Ch 29:19; 2Th 2:3.
Or, “what is killed without draining its blood.”
Lit., “centurions,” officers each in command of 100 soldiers.
Or, “assembly of elders; presbytery.” Gr., pre·sby·teʹri·on.
Or, “hear understandingly,” as Paul did in vs 7.
Or, “wash your sins away and call.”
“I fell into a trance,” אAB; J13,14,17,22, “Jehovah’s hand was upon me”; J18, “Jehovah’s spirit clothed me.”
Or, “stretched him out with the straps.”
That is, about 9 p.m., counting from sunset.
“I brought him down into their Sanhedrin,” P74אAVgSyp; B* omits.

P74אABVg omit the following from vss 6-8, which read, according to VgcSyh,pArm: “and wanted to judge according to our Law. (7) But Lysias the military commander came up and with great force took him out of our hands, (8) commanding his accusers to come to you.”
“I am rendering sacred service.” Gr., la·treuʹo; J17,18(Heb.), ʼaniʹ ʽo·vedhʹ, “I am serving (worshiping).” See Ex 3:12 ftn.
“Resurrection.” Gr., a·naʹsta·sin, “raising up; standing up” (from a·naʹ, “up,” and staʹsis, “standing”); Lat., re·sur·rec·ti·oʹnem.
Lit., “the chiliarch,” a commander of 1,000 soldiers.
Lit., “the centurion,” a commander of 100 soldiers.
That is, of Judea, with Caesarea serving as the governor’s residence.
The sister of Herod Agrippa II, but living incestuously with him.
“Worship of the deity.” Lit., “dread of demons.” Gr., dei·si·dai·mo·niʹas; Lat., su·per·sti·ti·oʹne; J17,18, “service of their God.” See 17:22 ftn.
Or, “Augustus; the emperor.” Gr., Se·ba·stouʹ; Lat., Au·guʹsti. The title of Nero Caesar, the fourth in succession from Octavian who first held this title.
Or, “sect of our religion.” Lat., secʹtam noʹstrae re·li·gi·oʹnis.
Lit., “[voting] pebble.” Gr., pseʹphon. See Re 2:17 ftn, “Pebble.”
Or, “the centurion,” a commander of 100 soldiers.
Or, “looking along the southwest wind and along the northwest wind.”
“Euroaquilo.” Gr., Eu·ra·kyʹlon; Lat., eu·ro·aʹqui·lo; a northeast wind.
Two large shallow gulfs, full of shifting sandbanks, on the coast of Libya, North Africa.
Lit., “I am rendering sacred service.” Gr., la·treuʹo; J17(Heb.), ʼaniʹ ʽo·vedhʹ, “I serve (worship).” See Ex 3:12 ftn.
Then including what is now the Adriatic Sea, the Ionian Sea and that part of the Mediterranean Sea between Sicily and Crete.
“Fathoms.” Gr., or·gui·asʹ. A fathom is commonly viewed as being four cubits (c. 1.8 m; 6 ft).

“Two hundred and seventy-six,” אItmssVgSyh,p; A, “two hundred and seventy-five”; B, “about seventy-six.” In WH the Gr. word ὡς (hos, “about”) is marked by superior half-brackets, and in the margin appears the Gr. word di·a·koʹsi·ai, “two hundred.” The copyist for B evidently made a mistake by combining the final Omega, ῳ (oi), of the preceding Gr. word, πλοίῳ (ploiʹoi), with the next letter, Sigma, ς (s), standing for 200, to form the Gr. word ὡς (hos, “about”). Hence the actual number is 276 instead of 76.
Lit., “affection for mankind.” Gr., phi·lan·thro·piʹan. Compare Tit 3:4 ftn.
Or, “Dioscuri,” the twin brothers Castor and Pollux.
אAB omit vs 29; ItmssVgc, “And when he had said this, the Jews went away, having a great deal of disputing among themselves.”
Or, “heralding.” Gr., ke·rysʹson; Lat., praeʹdi·cans. Compare Da 5:29 ftn, “Heralded.”
